answer_1.quote: Recent advances in pre-trained langauge models (PLMs) have made great impact on text generation research, especially when they are finetuned on downstream tasks such as summarization, data-to-text generation, long-question answering, etc.

answer_2.quote: For model evaluations we use ROUGE-1/2/L using Python rouge-score 0.0.4 version licensed under the Apache 2.0 License. We use the default ROUGE script rouge.py from the GEM evaluation shared task. All other metrics are adopted from their linked corresponding papers. We use the official evaluation script for BLEU, METEOR (Lavie and Agarwal, 2007), NIST, TER, MoverScore, BERTScore.

answer_4.quote: To evaluate the generated text from our proposed methods against baseline models, we ask human annotators to rate generations on five criteria: faithfulness (consistent with the context), relevance (captures key-points), grammaticality, coherence (form a cohesive whole), and overall quality (informative).
answer_4.guideline: Judges are shown the original document, the ground truth summary and two model summaries in random order and compare head-to-head on each criterion, choosing a winner or marking as same.
